title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000030: three declared forward references name work products the corpus has never authored, and no rule resolves a payload-field id

revision_history.description: Raised while remediating finding FB2-REV-FND-000023. The corpus-wide reference sweep that pass required surfaced three references to ids that no record defines. They are not typos - each names a work product the plan declares and the corpus has not written - so they cannot be repaired by correcting a value, and they are recorded here rather than deleted or satisfied by inventing a record.

evidence: docs/artifacts/tools/check_references.py resolves every id-shaped string in every corpus and scenario record against the artifact index, the source registry, the assumption registries, the link registries and the parameter registries. After the FB2-SAF-SCO-000001 typo was corrected under FB2-REV-FND-000023, three references remained unresolved in four places: (1) FB2-SW-DSN-000001's decomposition[2].child_id names FB2-SW-DSN-000004, and only FB2-SW-DSN-000001..000003 exist - the same reference appears in the as_is and the synthetic_reference copies of the record; (2) FB2-PIM-IMP-000003 is named by project-plan.json work_breakdown[WBS-008].deliverable_records[4] and by measurement-plan.json metrics[MET-06].linked_improvement_records[0], and only FB2-PIM-IMP-000001 and FB2-PIM-IMP-000002 exist. None of these ids has ever existed, so unlike FB2-SAF-SCO-000001 they are not transcriptions of an id that was renamed.
impact: A reader following FB2-SW-DSN-000001's decomposition arrives at a design element that does not exist, and a reader following WBS-008's deliverables or MET-06's linked improvements arrives at a process improvement that does not exist. The traceability report's coverage count for review and for planned deliverables is computed over ids that include these, so the denominators contain entries a reader cannot resolve. The risk of the reverse error is the larger one: because a payload-field id is never resolved by the link validator or by any other rule, a reader cannot tell an intentional forward reference to planned-but-unwritten work from a typo, and this corpus has now demonstrated both - FB2-SAF-SCO-000001 was a typo and these three are not.
root_cause: The corpus declares work products in planning artefacts before the artefacts themselves exist, and no record distinguishes a declared-forward reference from a broken one. The link validator only resolves ids expressed as links; a free-string id in a payload field is outside every rule's reach. The gap is structural, not clerical: three separate planning references were written forward and none of them says so.
resolution:
STILL OPEN, and deliberately so. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: FB2-SW-DSN-000004 and FB2-PIM-IMP-000003 are still absent from the artifact index. Nothing was authored to close it and nothing should have been.

WHY IT WAS NOT CLOSED. Writing FB2-SW-DSN-000004 would mean inventing the architecture of an AFE driver child element, and writing FB2-PIM-IMP-000003 would mean inventing the content of a process-improvement cycle. No source, parameter, assumption or analysis in this corpus constrains either, so authoring them would be fabrication wearing a record id, which master prompt section 14 forbids by name. The two references were not typos - unlike FB2-SAF-SCO-000001, which was, and which was corrected under FB2-REV-FND-000023 - so they cannot be closed the way that one was.

WHAT IS IN PLACE. docs/artifacts/tools/check_references.py resolves every id-shaped string in every corpus and scenario record against the artifact index, the source registry, the assumption registries, the link registries and the parameter registries, and prints anything that does not resolve. Both ids carry an explicit entry in that tool's KNOWN_BROKEN_ALLOWED declared-forward allowlist, so the tool reports them as declared-forward rather than passing them silently. That is the difference between this class of defect and FB2-SAF-SCO-000001: the tool can now tell a planned-but-unwritten reference from a typo, which is what stopped the same mistyped value appearing in two records before.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT, precisely. A decision by an owner who knows the intended architecture and the intended improvement cycle: either author the two records from real design and process input, or mark the three references as planned-not-yet-authored on the face of the records that carry them so a reader is not left resolving a dangling id. Both are engineering and planning decisions. No automated pass may take either, and this corpus is not in a position to invent the content either would need. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.
